title: Proptest scaffolding for SIMD-vs-scalar equivalence
description:
Add a shared proptest helper that every new SIMD kernel uses to prove bit-exact equivalence with the scalar baseline. Without this scaffolding, each kernel author writes their own equivalence test — guaranteeing inconsistent coverage.

## Background

Every Tier A–D task ships a SIMD kernel that must produce bit-exact output equal to the scalar reference for all valid inputs. The helper at `crates/gf2-core/tests/simd_equiv/mod.rs` provides:

1. `assert_simd_matches_scalar<F, G, T>(scalar: F, simd: G, gen: impl Strategy<Value = T>)` — runs proptest over the generator, asserts bit-exact equality.
2. Word-boundary helper: `WORD_BOUNDARY_LENGTHS: &[usize] = &[0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129, 255, 256, 257]`. Each new SIMD kernel adds a `#[test]` iterating this list.
3. Alignment helper: produces `&[u64]` slices at offsets $0..7$ within an over-allocated buffer to exercise unaligned paths.
4. A demo unit test exercising the helper against `LogicalFns::xor_fn` (scalar) vs. AVX2 `xor_inplace_avx2` (SIMD).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Helper compiles; fast-tier nextest passes.
- [hard] Demo test catches a deliberate one-bit mutation in the scalar fn (mutation-tested to verify the test actually tests).
- [hard] No new dependencies beyond what `gf2-core` and `proptest` already provide.
